clue.text: Aquatints?

parts.note: read literally as tints made with water, pictures painted in pigments thinned with water rather than the etching process

explanation.surface: A one-word query about a kind of etched print.
explanation.walkthrough: An aquatint is really an etching technique; the question mark invites reading it as 'water tints', paintings in water-based paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings done in water-thinned pigments are, punningly, tints of the aqua kind.

clue.text: Lift arm defensively-as a salute?

parts.note: raising an arm to fend off a blow, which might be mistaken for a salute, is to repel or deflect an attack

explanation.surface: Someone raises an arm to protect themselves, and it looks like a salute.
explanation.definitionFit: To fend off or repel a blow is what a raised protective arm does.

clue.text: Raise hat to a South African bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts its letters so they read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Doffing one's hat to a bird met in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' turns HAT upwards in this down entry to give TAH; then A.
explanation.definitionFit: The taha is a weaver bird of southern Africa, a species of bishop bird.

clue.text: Understanding how to tap wine

parts.note: to tap is to knock lightly, to rap
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A lesson in broaching a cask of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapport is a close, sympathetic relationship in which people understand each other.

clue.text: Leg block while doing sentry-go

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
a guard is something that blocks or shields

explanation.surface: Instructions for a soldier: brace your leg while standing sentry.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field (behind the batsman's legs) is also the on side, so 'Leg' gives ON. 'Sentry-go' is old British slang for sentry duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry on duty is watchful and alert, standing guard against any threat.

clue.text: Ring up tiny cripple, but don't include him

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' lifts the name so its letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Tiny Tim is the crippled boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

explanation.surface: Phone the little invalid, but leave him out of the plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TIM in this down entry to give MIT, after O. Tiny Tim is the lame child of the Cratchit family in A Christmas Carol.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out is to fail to include it.

clue.text: Seek another loan to improve the picture

definitions.meaning: to touch someone is slang for asking them for money, so doing it again is a second touch
to make small corrections to a painting or photograph

explanation.surface: A borrower who wants a further advance in order to restore a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch' in British slang means to ask someone for a loan ('touch him for a fiver').
explanation.definitionFit: Artists and photographers make small corrective touches to enhance an image; asking for a second loan is a repeated touch.

clue.text: Maybe if not so careless they could get regular work (6, 7) 8100l tales of darkness in the Middle East

definitions.text: Maybe if not so careless they could get regular work

parts.words: Maybe if not so careless they could get regular work
parts.note: careless suggests offhand, so the people meant are offhand or occasional labourers, hired by the day without steady jobs

explanation.surface: A lament that slapdash labourers would find steady employment if they tried harder.
explanation.walkthrough: Casual here means occasional, not careless: these labourers are hired as needed, and the clue pretends they lack regular work only through slackness. The rest of the line as held is the next clue run in by the OCR.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporary labourers without permanent contracts are employed on an irregular basis.

clue.text: 1001 tales of darkness in the Middle East

definitions.meaning: the collection of stories told by Scheherazade over a thousand and one nights
evenings spent in Arabia, nighttime in that region

explanation.surface: A thousand and one stories of shadowy deeds in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous story collection is set in the Arab world, and its title literally means nighttime in Arabia.

clue.text: Maybe a hovercraft on the skyline

definitions.text: Maybe a hovercraft on the skyline

parts.words: Maybe a hovercraft on the skyline
parts.note: something that hovers high in the sky, a craft that floats in the air, rather than the cushion vessel

explanation.surface: A hovercraft glimpsed on the horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: A hovercraft skims water on an air cushion; read as 'a craft that hovers', a blimp or dirigible fits, seen up in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirigible floats in the air, so it is a craft that hovers above the skyline.

clue.text: Note rubbish is typical of tinsel

parts.note: G is one of the musical notes A to G
litter is discarded rubbish

explanation.surface: Musing that sparkly decorations are just rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel's characteristic quality is sparkle, shiny bright twinkle.

clue.text: Supported by evidence that switch is topsy-turvy

definitions.meaning: resting on top of, as a cup sits on a saucer
a British light switch is off when pushed up, so one reading up and on at once is upside down

explanation.surface: Proof that a switch has been fitted upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a switch is pressed down to turn it on; one that is 'up' and 'on' must have been installed the wrong way up.
explanation.definitionFit: Resting on something means being held up by it, as a preposition.

clue.text: A very long way to this point

definitions.meaning: such a great distance
up until now

explanation.surface: Someone says they have come a long distance up to here.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'such a distance' and 'until now'.

clue.text: Weep copiously when returning to plant this

indicators.note: something returning comes back, so the word for weeping is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to blub is to cry noisily

explanation.surface: Advice to sob heavily while planting something in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when returning' reverses BLUB, British slang for crying.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulips and daffodils grow from a rounded underground storage organ that gardeners plant.

clue.text: It goes around both ways

indicators.note: the word reads the same whichever way it is taken, forwards or backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something that spins round in either direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both ways' says the answer is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter's spinning blade assembly revolves on its axis.

clue.text: South African place of birth

definitions.meaning: a former province on South Africa's east coast
relating to being born

explanation.surface: Someone's birthplace in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things connected with being born, and it is also a region in South Africa.

clue.text: Anti-socialist slogan which is omitted

definitions.meaning: a chant demanding the left-wing party be thrown from power
not included

explanation.surface: A political chant aimed at socialists, which was cut from the speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not included has been passed over; the same words could be a call to eject the political left.

clue.text: Money for Greek drama about honourable companion

indicators.note: the play goes about, that is surrounds, the companion

parts.note: taken as written
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Funding a Greek tragedy about a distinguished friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CH inside DRAMA. CH is a British honour, Companion of Honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The old currency of Greece before the euro was this coin.

clue.text: Weird work for handymen

parts.note: strange jobs read differently as the miscellaneous small tasks a handyman takes on

explanation.surface: Handymen being given bizarre tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weird' suggests strangeness, but odd here means miscellaneous, small assorted tasks.
explanation.definitionFit: Handymen do assorted small repair tasks, which are punningly 'weird work'.

clue.text: Butter fingers for the application of eye lotion

definitions.meaning: a clumsy person who keeps letting things fall

definitions.text: for the application of eye lotion
definitions.meaning: a small pipette that dispenses liquid one bead at a time

explanation.surface: A clumsy person trying to put drops in their eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butterfingers' is a British jibe for someone who fumbles catches.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy person lets things fall, and a pipette lets liquid fall drop by drop into the eye.

clue.text: Sort of betting aspect which adds a bit of glitter

parts.note: SP is the starting price in horse-race betting
an angle is a viewpoint or aspect

explanation.surface: A gambling angle that adds a touch of sparkle.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, starting price, is the odds at the start of a race in British bookmaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequin is a small shiny disc sewn on clothes, one tiny piece of sparkle.

clue.text: Punish, even though many hurry

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
to hasten is to hurry

explanation.surface: Someone protests at being disciplined even though lots of people are rushing.
explanation.definitionFit: To discipline or rebuke someone in order to correct them.

clue.text: One imprisoned in fortress in Spain

indicators.note: a prisoner is shut inside walls, so the first letter goes within the stronghold word

parts.note: a castle is a fortress
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single prisoner locked up in a Spanish fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned in' puts I inside CASTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The old kingdom at the heart of the Iberian peninsula is a region of that country.

clue.text: He may travel to ancient city and sit in ruins

parts.note: taken as written
Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia

indicators.note: something in ruins is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller visits an old city and sits among its ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ruins' scrambles SIT to IST, after TO and UR.
explanation.definitionFit: A holidaymaker travels for pleasure and sightseeing.

clue.text: Speed of ship going to tie up

definitions.meaning: a nautical mile per hour, the unit sailors use
to fasten with a tied loop

explanation.surface: A ship's pace before mooring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships measure speed in nautical miles per hour, and the same word means to fasten a rope.

clue.text: Turning over a slab of wood

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the words are read from the end back to the start

explanation.surface: Flipping a slab of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning over' reverses A SLAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A very light timber from a tropical American tree, used for models.

clue.text: Psychologist put Pole in jug

indicators.note: the pole is placed within the vessel, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: Someone drops a Polish man into a jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside JUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Jung was the Swiss founder of analytical psychology.

clue.text: Notice how to make a name for oneself

definitions.meaning: a board or placard giving information
to write one's signature

explanation.surface: A notice explaining how to become famous.
explanation.definitionFit: A posted placard gives information, and writing your signature is literally putting your name down.

clue.text: Sword drawn from orange peel

indicators.note: drawn from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A blade pulled out of a piece of fruit skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn from' also suits a sword drawn from its sheath.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencing weapon with a stiff blade, used in competition.

clue.text: Excellent way of ruining clothes

definitions.meaning: dated British slang for splendid
tearing fabric

explanation.surface: Someone praising a method of wrecking garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned British slang for splendid, and tearing fabric spoils a garment.

clue.text: Am the type to leave a mark

parts.note: with the speaker understood, 'am' is the contraction of I am
print is printed type

explanation.surface: Someone boasting they are the sort to make an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Am' as the speaker's 'I'm'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp or impress a mark on a surface.

clue.text: Creeping rent disturbed George IV before he succeeded

indicators.note: letters disturbed are thrown out of order, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rising rents troubled a monarch before he came to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges CREEPING RENT. George IV ruled for his ill father from 1811 until he became king in 1820.
explanation.definitionFit: Before his accession he ruled on behalf of George III, giving the Regency period its name.
